summary: Edit an existing VM in place on its General tab: PUT /api/v1/vms/{id} queues a vm-update command with the full definition at revision current + 1; Core applies live what a running guest can take and redefines a stopped one; every VM has a CD drive; the journal keeps revisions and reports the current definition. API impact: new contract (updateVM, vm-update, vm-update-v1) and changed contract (VMCreateSpec.revision, effective MACs in the VM list, media boot order without media, current definitions in Inventory.managed.vms).

guide.reason: New operator workflow for editing a VM; creation and power pages no longer say editing is unavailable. The create page's status paragraph was updated too; it was swept into commit 96d3288 by a concurrent session before this record landed.

api.reason: New updateVM operation, vm-update command and vm-update-v1 capability; VMCreateSpec.revision, effective MACs in the VM list, media boot order without media, current definitions in Inventory.managed.vms.

state.reason: Every revision of a VM's definition is a vm-update journal entry on the pool master's Nex Core; the Controller mirrors the current one.
state.record: Managed journal entries under the agent state directory managed-vms/<operation>.json of kind vm-update (full VMCreateSpec with revision, disk paths, targets, retained files, expected XML); Inventory.managed.vms reports the highest succeeded revision per VM, which a fresh Controller adopts as the VM's definition and an existing one refreshes its mirror from.

verification.method: go test -race ./... ; python3 -m unittest tests.test_api_contract (21 OK); python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check; npm run typecheck && npm run build; python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree; tests/integration/vm_edit_browser.py against the simulated host (3 checks, 5 captures inspected); tests/integration/vm_edit_lab.py against a disposable copy of the nested-KVM lab host with real libvirt (all six steps passed; see docs/qa/vm-edit/checks.md and lab-results.json).
